quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #10
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Four lanes of traffic ahead.
A divided highway ahead.
Two-way traffic ahead.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about conditions just ahead. This sign warns you that you are leaving a one-way highway and entering a two-way highway.

questions.question: At night, an oncoming car has high beams on and you cannot see the road ahead. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the other vehicle from the corner of your eye.

questions.question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter the situation.

questions.question: Before driving, remove snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.explanation: You must be able to see clearly through all windows. Clear snow, ice, and frost from all windows and mirrors before driving.

questions.question: When can you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the vehicle in front moves to the right for you.
When the yellow line on your side is broken.
When the yellow line on the opposite side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side is broken.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means traffic on that side may pass if it is safe. A solid yellow line means you cannot pass.

questions.question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed only from the side with the dashed line.
questions.explanation: When there is a dashed line and a solid line, only traffic next to the dashed line may cross to pass. Traffic next to the solid line cannot pass.

questions.question: What does a double solid yellow line in the center of the road mean for passing?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed only from your direction.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double yellow lines mean no traffic from either direction may cross the center to pass.

questions.question: What should you do at a traffic light that is not working?

options.text: Stop completely and yield the right-of-way before entering.
If the intersection is clear, you do not need to stop.
Drive quickly through to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely and yield the right-of-way before entering.
questions.explanation: At a broken traffic light, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Come to a complete stop, look carefully, and yield before entering.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Right turn on red is allowed with caution.
All traffic must turn right at the next intersection.

questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. This sign means right turns are prohibited.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Winding road ahead.
Do not enter.
Pedestrian crossing.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you about a winding road ahead.

questions.question: Which lane should you be in to make a left turn from a one-way street?

options.text: The lane closest to the left curb.
The lane closest to the center of the street.
The lane closest to the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to the left curb.
questions.explanation: When turning, use the lane that points in the direction you want to go. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: Before entering a curve, you should:

options.text: Turn on your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.explanation: Slow down when approaching curves, hills with limited visibility, slippery roads, or areas with pedestrians and animals. You can drive slower than the posted speed limit for safety, but never faster.

questions.question: Drivers must obey instructions from:

options.text: Security guards in parking lots.
Other drivers with broken-down vehicles on the road.
Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.

questions.explanation: You must obey flaggers at construction sites. They are there to keep drivers and workers safe.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing, you must:

options.text: Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings, like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials.
Watch for multiple trains.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Approach all railroad crossings with extreme caution. Cross only when you know no train is coming from either direction. Watch for vehicles that must stop at crossings, like school buses and hazmat trucks.

questions.question: In heavy fog, you should slow down and:

options.text: Turn on your emergency flashers.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beam light reflects off moisture and causes glare, making it harder to see. Some vehicles have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: If the road ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Turn around and find another route. Do not drive through flooded areas.
Drive through the center of the road only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn around and find another route. Do not drive through flooded areas.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Water may hide hazards even if it looks shallow. Turn around and find another route.

questions.question: Signs with orange backgrounds mean:

options.text: General warnings.
Construction and maintenance work ahead.
Traffic rules and regulations.

questions.explanation: Orange signs are used only for construction and maintenance warnings.

questions.question: A safe driver should:

options.text: Assume all drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Assume most drivers follow right-of-way rules.
Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to give up the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: Do not assume you have the right-of-way. Consider the situation at every intersection. Yield your right-of-way to prevent collisions.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck to stop.
Other drivers to slow down.

questions.explanation: Large trucks take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Pass as slowly as possible.
Drive at the same speed as the other vehicle.
Pass quickly and safely.

questions.explanation: Pass quickly to return to normal driving. Return to your lane only when you can see both of the other vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What should you do to avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after you start going down a steep hill.
Speed up when entering curves and slow down when leaving them.
Slow down before you enter curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve because you cannot see what is ahead. Braking while turning may cause you to skid.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the left side of the cab.
Both on the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both on the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have much larger blind spots than cars. The driver cannot see your car behind the truck. If you drive too close behind a truck, you cannot see traffic ahead. If the driver cannot see your face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: When turning left, drivers must yield to:

options.text: Cars passing them.
Cars coming toward them.
No one.

questions.explanation: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming traffic. You can only turn left when it is safe and does not interfere with oncoming cars.

questions.question: What do drivers need for interstate driving?

options.text: The ability to safely drive at higher speeds.
Constant alertness.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert at all times and be able to drive at high speeds.

questions.question: Which statement about seat belts is false?

options.text: They hold you in place during a crash.
They are not needed if your vehicle has an airbag.
They keep you from being thrown from the vehicle in an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not needed if your vehicle has an airbag.
questions.explanation: State law requires seat belts to be worn even with airbags. Airbags protect you from hitting the steering wheel, dashboard, and windshield. They do not protect you from side or rear crashes or rollovers. Airbags cannot keep you in your seat in these situations.
